readme: Andhra Pradesh citizen contact and grievance directory. Every entry was read off a government page and carries that page. Research pass 30 Aug 2026. Nothing here is transcribed from an aggregator, a directory site or a news report — a wrong helpline number is worse than a missing one.
warning: Most district collectorate phone numbers, most department phone numbers and emails, and every district's pre-2022 parent district are NOT in this file because no government page I could reach publishes them; they are null, and 'unavailable' says exactly which page a person in Andhra Pradesh should open to get them.

emergency.what_for: Reporting online financial fraud so the money trail can be frozen; complaint is then registered on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. Replaced the earlier number 155260.

grievance.name: PGRS / Mee Kosam - Andhra Pradesh Public Grievance Redressal System
grievance.what_for: The state's current one-stop public grievance platform. Described on the portal as 'a universal grievance redressal helpline that allows citizens to directly raise their issue to the Chief Minister's Office'. Use it to (a) register an individual or household-level grievance, (b) follow up on a registered grievance, (c) enquire about government services and schemes.
grievance.how_to_file: Online at https://pgrs.ap.gov.in or https://meekosam.ap.gov.in (authentication is by OTP to the Aadhaar-linked mobile number, with UIDAI verification and consent); by the mobile app; or in person at the Collectorate grievance session held on Mondays.

grievance.name: Spandana
grievance.what_for: Andhra Pradesh's public grievance platform as described on district collectorate sites - 'a public problem solving platform' for citizen petitions to any state, district or zonal official.
grievance.how_to_file: Submit through the Spandana citizen portal, or hand the application to any state/district/zonal level official; you get a receipt with an application number, and the application is scanned and forwarded to the responsible officer.

grievance.name: Grama/Ward Sachivalayam citizen services portal (AP Seva)
grievance.what_for: The single window for applying for state services at the village or ward secretariat - certificates, welfare scheme applications, land and civil-supplies services. This is the first rung of almost every escalation ladder below.
grievance.how_to_file: Walk in to your Grama Sachivalayam (village) or Ward Sachivalayam (urban) with the required documents and get an acknowledgement with an application number, or apply online. The former URL https://vswsonline.ap.gov.in now redirects (HTTP 302) to https://apseva.ap.gov.in.
grievance.source_url: https://igod.gov.in/sg/AP/SPMA/organizations ; observed 302 redirect from https://vswsonline.ap.gov.in/#/home to https://apseva.ap.gov.in/

grievance.name: MeeSeva (integrated services delivery gateway)
grievance.what_for: Counter and online delivery of certificates and government services in Andhra Pradesh.
grievance.how_to_file: At a MeeSeva centre, or online through the citizen portal at https://onlineap.meeseva.gov.in/CitizenPortal/UserInterface/Citizen/Home.aspx

grievance.name: CPGRAMS - Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (Government of India)
grievance.what_for: Grievances against central government ministries, departments and organisations, and against state governments where the state is onboarded. Available 24x7.
grievance.how_to_file: Online at pgportal.gov.in, through the CPGRAMS mobile app (Android/iOS), through UMANG, or at a Common Service Centre (CSC). Grievances sent by email are not entertained - filing on the portal is mandatory.

grievance.name: Andhra Pradesh Information Commission (RTI second appeal and complaint)
grievance.what_for: Second appeals and complaints under the Right to Information Act, 2005 against AP public authorities, after the departmental first appeal fails.
grievance.how_to_file: Not verified - the Commission's site could not be fetched from this environment.

grievance.name: Institution of Lokayukta, Andhra Pradesh
grievance.what_for: Complaints of maladministration, abuse of office and allegations against public functionaries, under the Andhra Pradesh Lokayukta Act, 1983 (the site names the Act and refers to an Investigation Wing).
grievance.how_to_file: Use Form I / Form II (available in English and Telugu) from the Downloads section of the site, together with the 'How to complain' guide.

grievance.name: Anti-Corruption Bureau, Andhra Pradesh
grievance.what_for: Complaints of bribery and corruption by public servants in Andhra Pradesh, including trap cases and disproportionate assets.
grievance.how_to_file: Toll-free 14400 ('Register Complaint against corruption Toll Free Number' as published on AP district collectorate helpline pages). The ACB website itself could not be fetched from this environment, so its online complaint route is unverified.

grievance.name: Andhra Pradesh Vigilance Commission
grievance.what_for: Vigilance oversight of AP government departments and public servants.

grievance.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP)
grievance.what_for: Reporting cybercrime, including financial fraud, cyber-stalking and crimes against women and children. Run by the Ministry of Home Affairs. Also carries a 'Suspect Repository' where a citizen can check mobile numbers, emails and URLs linked to cybercriminals.
grievance.how_to_file: Call 1930 immediately for financial fraud (so the transaction trail can be frozen), then register on the portal via 'Register a Complaint' and select 'FINANCIAL FRAUD' for money-loss cases.

grievance.name: National Consumer Helpline (NCH 2.0), Department of Consumer Affairs
grievance.what_for: Pre-litigation consumer grievance against a business - refunds, defective goods, deficient services.
grievance.how_to_file: Call 1915 (8AM to 8PM, 17 languages), or use the portal, the NCH app, UMANG, WhatsApp +918800001915, or SMS. Documents can be uploaded to the complaint.

grievance.name: Andhra Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (SCDRC)
grievance.what_for: Statutory consumer adjudication in Andhra Pradesh - appeals from District Consumer Commissions and original complaints above the district pecuniary limit.
grievance.how_to_file: Not verified - the Commission's site could not be fetched from this environment. Online filing for consumer complaints nationally is through the NCDRC's e-Daakhil portal.

grievance.name: Vidyut Ombudsman, Andhra Pradesh
grievance.what_for: Final appellate forum for an electricity consumer whose grievance was not settled by the DISCOM's Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum.
grievance.how_to_file: Not verified - the page rendered no readable body content from this environment.

escalations.law: The Andhra Pradesh Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 (Act No. 6 of 2018). Verified from the Government of India's India Code repository. Its scheme: s.5 - the Government notifies, by notification, which public services are covered and the 'stipulated time limit' for each; s.2(i) defines 'stipulated time limit' as 'the maximum time to provide the service by the public authority'; s.6 - 'The Public Authority shall designate Officer/Officers for providing Public Services under this Act' (the Designated Officer); s.9 - 'Every Designated Officer who fails to deliver the public service to a person within the stipulated time shall be liable to pay compensation to the applicant at such rates as may be prescribed'; s.10 and s.11 provide for an appeal to an Appellate Authority and revision by the Government. IMPORTANT: the Act itself fixes no days for any service - the actual number of days for each service comes from the Government notification under s.5, which I could not locate on a government page. Source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/9072/1/apps_delivery_guarantee_act%2c_2017.pdf (act page: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/9072)

escalations.law: The Andhra Pradesh Public Services Delivery Guarantee Act, 2017 (Act No. 6 of 2018). Verified from the Government of India's India Code repository. Its scheme: s.5 - the Government notifies, by notification, which public services are covered and the 'stipulated time limit' for each; s.2(i) defines 'stipulated time limit' as 'the maximum time to provide the service by the public authority'; s.6 - 'The Public Authority shall designate Officer/Officers for providing Public Services under this Act' (the Designated Officer); s.9 - 'Every Designated Officer who fails to deliver the public service to a person within the stipulated time shall be liable to pay compensation to the applicant at such rates as may be prescribed'; s.10 and s.11 provide for an appeal to an Appellate Authority and revision by the Government. IMPORTANT: the Act itself fixes no days for any service - the actual number of days for each service comes from the Government notification under s.5, which I could not locate on a government page. Source: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/9072/1/apps_delivery_guarantee_act%2c_2017.pdf (act page: https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/9072)

escalations.problem: Police - how to file an FIR, and what to do if a police station refuses to register one

steps.office: The police station with jurisdiction - give the information orally or in writing. Dial 100 (or 112) to bring police to you; AP Police also send officers to the complainant in cases involving women and children rather than requiring a station visit.
steps.what_to_bring: A written complaint signed by you (AP Police state: 'In case of registration of a case, a written complaint along with the signature is necessary as per law'). Carry ID and any evidence; ask for and keep the FIR number and a free copy of the FIR.
steps.time_limit: An FIR must be registered without preliminary inquiry where the information discloses a cognizable offence.

steps.office: If the offence happened outside that station's jurisdiction - insist on a ZERO FIR. The station must register it, write 'Zero FIR' in the FIR number column and forward it to the station with jurisdiction through the Superintendent of Police.
steps.what_to_bring: Same as above; note the officer's name and the date/time you attended.
steps.time_limit: Immediate - no preliminary inquiry is permitted.

steps.office: REFUSAL - REMEDY 1: send the substance of the information in writing, by post, to the District Superintendent of Police (in a city commissionerate, the Commissioner of Police / DCP). Under BNSS s.173(4) the District Superintendent of Police may order investigation of a cognizable offence, and on such an order the station house officer must register the FIR.
steps.what_to_bring: A written complaint plus proof that you approached the station (dated acknowledgement, registered-post receipt, or the date and officer's name).
steps.time_limit: Not stated in the source.
steps.portal: Also lodge it in parallel on https://pgrs.ap.gov.in and, for a cyber offence, https://cybercrime.gov.in

steps.office: REFUSAL - REMEDY 2: apply to the jurisdictional Judicial Magistrate. Under BNSS s.175(3) a court may order investigation of a cognizable offence, and on that direction the officer must register an FIR. No preliminary inquiry is permitted and investigation must proceed without delay.
steps.what_to_bring: Your written complaint, the proof of refusal, and an affidavit; the application is made to the Magistrate having jurisdiction.
steps.time_limit: Not stated in the source.

steps.office: Parallel routes: State Human Rights Commission / NHRC (14433) for police misconduct; Anti-Corruption Bureau on 14400 if a bribe was demanded; the Superintendent of Police's weekly grievance day.
steps.what_to_bring: Everything above.
steps.time_limit: Not published on a page I could read.

escalations.law: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 46 of 2023) - s.173 (information in cognizable cases, including s.173(4): order of the District Superintendent of Police) and s.175(3) (a court may order investigation). Verified from a state police department circular published on a gov.in domain: https://megpolice.gov.in/sites/default/files/circular-no.3-2024-first-information-report.pdf . The BNSS text itself is at https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/20099/1/A202346.pdf but the relevant sections were beyond the portion of that PDF I could read.

steps.office: Write to the business - its published grievance/nodal officer - and keep the reply or the proof of no reply.
steps.what_to_bring: Invoice or receipt, warranty card, payment proof, the advertisement or promise you relied on, and your written complaint with a date.
steps.time_limit: Not published on a page I could read.

steps.office: National Consumer Helpline - call 1915 (8AM to 8PM, 17 languages), or use consumerhelpline.gov.in, the NCH app, UMANG, SMS, or WhatsApp +918800001915. Upload your documents.
steps.what_to_bring: The documents above and the company's reply.
steps.time_limit: Not stated on the portal.

steps.office: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for your district - a formal, adjudicated complaint.
steps.what_to_bring: Complaint with an affidavit, the documents above, and the prescribed fee. Online filing nationally is through the NCDRC's e-Daakhil portal.
steps.time_limit: Not verified from a government page.

steps.office: Andhra Pradesh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission - appeal from the District Commission, and original complaints above the district pecuniary limit.
steps.what_to_bring: The District Commission's order and the record.
steps.time_limit: Not verified.

steps.office: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), then the Supreme Court.
steps.what_to_bring: The State Commission's order.
steps.time_limit: Not verified.
